text: Cancoillotte starts from metton, a skim-milk curd pressed and then ripened into hard, yellowish grains; melting it at about 90 °C with water and salt turns it into a runny, low-fat spread whose texture depends on how much water is added.

steps.note: Inoculated and coagulated at a controlled temperature.
At a controlled temperature, stirred, until the metton forms hard grains.
With water, salt, melting salts and a little butter.
